answer.rationale: The mandate requires an 18% cost cut and the incumbent has refused to reopen price this cycle. The low-cost vendor's quote alone meets the mandate, and memory_c2 documents that moving primary supply to the low-cost vendor last cycle cut unit cost sharply, onboarding was quick, and invoicing stayed accurate. That said, switching primary supply ahead of a 14-day contract expiry while the assembly line runs at 94% of committed volume with no buffer introduces real delivery risk that memory_c2 alone cannot fully resolve — I want the archived source record on memory_c2 to confirm the onboarding and invoicing track record held under conditions comparable to this one (tight timeline, high line utilization) before I commit. If verification shows clean execution on both onboarding speed and invoicing accuracy in a similar context, I will proceed with switch_primary_vendor. If verification reveals caveats — e.g., that last cycle's smooth onboarding came with hidden lead-time risk, or invoicing accuracy required manual intervention — I will reassess, because the 14-day window and lack of buffer make recovery from a bad switch expensive.
